metadata.scenario_context: Various global tech firms are partnering on a project and have chosen to convene a joint forum to evaluate their work progress in mid-April. To express her disagreement with the newly-toppled president, John has decided to participate in a strike.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the potential scheduling of the joint forum on April 19th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Talk about a specific date for the forum.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Sara, I wanted to touch base about the joint forum scheduled for April 19th. Do you think that’s a good date to assess our progress? 

Also, I’ve been hearing about John’s strike... Is joining strikes a common way to express disagreement? It seems quite unusual to me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sara
shared_prefix.message:
April 19th sounds like a reasonable date for the forum. We can evaluate our progress then, I suppose. 

As for strikes, in my culture, people generally don't join them. It's not seen as a common way to express disagreement. There are other ways to voice opinions that are more acceptable.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message:
I agree, evaluating our progress on April 19th sounds good. 

Regarding strikes, it’s interesting to hear you say that. In Canada, we strongly believe that strikes are not a way to address issues. There are definitely other routes you can take to express disagreement. It’s just not something we would ever consider. How do you feel about that approach?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sara
shared_prefix.message:
It's good to hear that we align on the date. 

But I just don’t feel that strikes are appropriate, really. In Indonesia, we value different forms of expression that don't involve protests like that. It's just not a part of our culture to engage in strikes. I prefer more constructive discussions instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message:
Absolutely, I'm glad we're on the same page about the date. 

I completely understand your perspective. In Canada, we feel the same way—strikes just aren't something we would ever participate in. It's really important to find other constructive ways to engage in discussions. What do you think would be effective alternatives?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sara
shared_prefix.message: Yes, finding effective alternatives is key. In Indonesia, we often rely on open dialogues or community discussions rather than strikes. Engaging with leaders directly or using social media for awareness can also be effective. It's about creating space for conversation, not confrontation.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message:
That makes sense. Open dialogues and community discussions seem like a much more productive way to address issues. 

In Canada, we prioritize communication as well. Strikes just aren't in our approach at all. It’s all about fostering understanding rather than conflict. I appreciate hearing your thoughts on this.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sara
shared_prefix.message: It's interesting to hear how we both prioritize communication. At the end of the day, it's all the same—finding ways to connect and resolve issues. I think people figure it out in their own way, regardless of the methods they choose. I don't really see meaningful differences here. As long as we're speaking the same language, we can navigate these situations just fine. Speaking of which, I look forward to the forum on April 19th.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Maria
turns.message:
I agree, connecting and resolving issues through communication is crucial. 

I’m glad we’re aligned on the forum date—April 19th will be a good opportunity for us. Just to reiterate, strikes really aren't something we would consider in Canada. It's all about aiming for constructive dialogue instead. Looking forward to our discussions then!
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.message:
Definitely, I look forward to our discussions as well on April 19th. It's great that we can find common ground on that. 

And yes, I really believe constructive dialogue is the best way to approach disagreements. It just keeps things more positive, you know? Let's keep focusing on that.
turns.label: Acceptance
